channel.title: Liuwa Pod
channel.description: Liuwa Pod is a ten-minute daily news show made in Lusaka. Every morning, Tash and Bwalya take the stories that matter to Zambian households and businesses, from power and mining to the kwacha, fuel and food prices and the wider world, and work out why they happened and what they mean for you. Then Professor Grace Mumba drops in with a word of the day and a piece of maths anyone can follow. Every figure is sourced in the show notes. The hosts are synthetic voices; the facts are real and independently checked. Nothing on Liuwa Pod is financial advice. Made by Liuwa Tech.

item.title: Ep 5 · The week oil wouldn't stop, and the doubling that ate the clock
item.description:
A Week in 10 special on Independence Day. Oil has its third straight weekly gain and its highest close since April, so we separate what is confirmed in the Gulf from what is only claimed and look at what it means for the fuel review due around 31 Oct. We also check where php2shell, Kariba and the FRA stand, clarify two unconfirmed figures, explain why central banks move interest rates and ask whether the market is doubting AI. Professor Mumba brings the word asunder, an Olympic twist from 1964, and a sum in which the last doubling beats all the earlier ones.

item.title: Ep 4 · The squeeze, and the robot that switched off its own alarm
item.description:
Oil hits a five-month high after deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia while copper slides to a five-week low, and we work out why Zambia feels both ends, and test Iran's unverified ship claims. Plus php2shell turns from warning to attack, the FRA funding freeze, COMESA's Lusaka headquarters and the solar-versus-Kariba race; Kwacha Sense on hedging; the first Kumunda call with Ba Mwape and his low well; OpenAI's agents that switched off their own monitoring; and Professor Mumba on how an average can lie.

item.title: Ep 3 · The bug in the engine, and the hidden sum on your bank card
item.description:
Two critical flaws in PHP, the language under most of the world's websites, were found with AI help and patched in a rush; we explain them, test the claim that AI found them before attackers did, and say what Zambian website owners should ask their hosts. Plus oil jumps on Gulf attacks, a fertiliser plant breaks ground in Chilanga, Kansanshi beats its design, Kwacha Sense on dollar prices in disguise, a data-centre power mandate in Frontier, and Professor Mumba reveals the check digit on every bank card.

item.title: Ep 2 · Swap maize, not soldiers, and the shortcut that slows everyone down
item.description:
President Hichilema wants the region swapping maize instead of soldiers as COMESA meets in Harare, and we ask what happens in a bad rain year, given Zambia's own 2024 export ban. Plus oil near a five-month high, South Africa's growth downgrade and an inflation watch; Kwacha Sense explains what the inflation number measures; Tesla's results and its robot promises, with an unexpected visit from Mr Phiri; and Professor Mumba shows how a free shortcut can make every driver slower.

item.title: Ep 1 · Use it or lose it, and the house always wins
item.description:
President Hichilema tells mining licence holders to use it or lose it, and we work out why an idle licence costs jobs, plus the Auditor-General's uncollected mining penalties, Zambians in hiding in South Africa, and fuel prices. Kwacha Sense explains why high copper hasn't lifted the kwacha, Kalaba does a labelled Musk impression on SpaceX's results, and Professor Mumba proves the house always wins at roulette.
